{"edits": [], "notes": "No edits proposed. The only listed finding (app/api_errors.py:10, `@validator`) is already resolved in the current content: `no_spaces` uses `@field_validator("username")` with `@classmethod`, which matches the v2 guide. Nothing else in the file is a v1 API (`Field(..., min_length=3)`, `ValidationError`, `exc.errors()` are all v2-compatible).

The failing test `test_codes` is caused by v1-era message strings in `MESSAGE_CODES` (lines 18-23), not by any listed finding. Pydantic v2 emits different `msg` text, so the lookup in line 32 falls through to "INVALID":
- "field required" is v1. v2 emits "Field required" (capital F), so the case-sensitive `startswith` misses it and `username` gets INVALID instead of MISSING.
- "value is not a valid integer" is v1. v2 emits "Input should be a valid integer, unable to parse string as an integer", so `age` gets INVALID instead of NOT_AN_INTEGER.
- "ensure this value has at least" is v1. v2 emits "String should have at least 3 characters" for `min_length`, so TOO_SHORT would also miss.

The fix is to update the keys in `MESSAGE_CODES` to the v2 message text, or to match on `err["type"]` (for example "missing", "int_parsing", "string_too_short") instead of the message string. Both edits fall outside the lines tied to the findings, and the previous attempt's edits to those lines were rejected as out of scope. I did not propose them. Please raise a separate finding for the `error["msg"]` to `error["type"]` change, or widen the scope for these lines, and I will propose the edit."}
